answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on trades or earn reputation. A willow-market escrow releases the stake only after the identity completes a fable of independently verified deliveries; pearl-sized deposits are forfeited when audits expose coordinated duplicates. Sybils must therefore tie up real capital and risk losing it, while one attacker gains no cheap extra influence merely by minting accounts.
